entry.idea: Companies that hold both bank accounts and stablecoins have to juggle separate logins, wallets, and spreadsheets, so Lisk gives them one workspace for accounts, payments, and approvals that works across both.
entry.lesson: When your original market dries up, pivot into an adjacent, unglamorous problem, here reconciling different money rails, for a similar kind of customer.
entry.name: Lisk

growth.reason: The product just opened Early Access and no user or revenue numbers have been published.

market.reason: Useful mainly to companies that already hold both bank accounts and stablecoins, a real but still niche group today.

tech.reason: It links existing bank rails and stablecoin rails into one interface, solid engineering but not something a strong team couldn't rebuild in a year.

sources.title: The vacuum Lisk's exit leaves in Africa's Web3 funding
Lisk eyes organically-growing Web3 startups with $15m fund

entry.twist: Lisk used to be a Web3 platform backing blockchain startups in emerging markets, and it pivoted into this fiat-and-stablecoin money operations tool after pulling out of that business.
entry.who_pays: Finance teams and leaders, such as CFOs, controllers, and COOs, at companies that will pay to use the platform once it leaves Early Access.
entry.why_now: More businesses now hold stablecoins alongside normal bank accounts, but no single tool handles payments and approvals across both, so there is a gap to fill.
